activity.notes: Representative c.1275 Udupi intellectual point. Madhva's absolute chronology is disputed, commonly given either around 1199–1278 or 1238–1317; c.1275 lies within both broad reconstructions and is not presented as an exact event. Reference sources place Madhva's teaching and institutional activity at Udupi. Government historical survey places South Kanara, including the Udupi area, under Alupa administrative control through this period, with the Alupas acknowledging Hoysala suzerainty. ATLAS therefore uses the more local Alupa polity for active_in while explicitly preserving the overlordship context.

sources.citation_text: Routledge identifies Madhva as the founder of Dvaita Vedānta and gives the commonly used 1238?–1317? chronology.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com — Madhva
sources.citation_text: The reference places Madhva at Udupi, describes pupils and teaching there, and records his establishment of the principal Krishna temple at Udupi while noting chronology traditions.

sources.title: District Census Handbook, Dakshin Kannad — historical survey
sources.citation_text: The Government of India district history states that South Kanara remained under Alupa administrative control up to about 1400 and that the Alupas accepted Hoysala suzerainty during the relevant medieval period.
